page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head at the top centre; page number at the top left. Heading in capitals across the column, with a smaller subtitle below it. Then verse paragraphs with italic lines, a centred sub-heading and further verse. Short centred headings and verse follow. The final line, "Iphi-", is a catchword at the right below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.head: AD RIXOSOS CONIVGES, ET PARI NEQVITIA praeditos.

p.i: Perditus es, coniux tua perdita: moribus ambo, Nequitia, vitijs, improbitate pares. Quum sit idem ingenium vobis, mirabile dictu est Tanta quod in veftro iurgia coniugio.

main_text.head: Ad Impurum quendam.

p.i: Cur male-sanus Ibertota quos ante petebat Mente Geneuates horret adire locos? Nempe timet flammas, timet atri carceris vncum, Dilaceraturas carnificisque manus, Errat & ante oculos noctisque diesque Megaera, Errant, & in manibus debita vincla suis. Ah! fugis incassum furias, Alphonse, minantes: Tandem aderit capiti debita poena tuo.

main_text.head: Vox Cratetis Milesij.

p.i: Quaeris, invenire difficile quid sit? O quam difficile est, senem tyrannum!

main_text.head: Sat cito, si sat bene.

p.i: Hoc satis est, metam maturo attingere cursu. Quae satis acta bene est res satis acta cito est.

page.notes: The first verse line of the first poem is printed "Perdis es"-type forms as scanned; the letters in the heading "NEQVITIA" are set with a tailed Q. Several lines are damaged at the right edge; "Iphi-" is the catchword. Some words in the italic verse are doubtful (e.g. "male-sanus", "vncum", "Mente Geneuates") due to type wear and show-through; these were read as best as possible without guessing further.
